$comment: The spine. `chapters` is null wherever the count has not been taken from the book itself — `npm run content:check` reports those as a work queue. Do not fill them in from fan wikis; several are AI-generated and demonstrably wrong. Floor accents are not here either — they come from data/book-colors.json, which holds each book's own colour as stated on mattdinniman.com.

books.title: Dungeon Crawler Carl
books.blurb: Earth is foreclosed on, and the only humans left standing are the ones who happened to be outside. Carl goes down into the dungeon barefoot, carrying a cat.

books.title: Carl's Doomsday Scenario
books.blurb: The Over City is the first floor that behaves like a place rather than a level — and Carl picks up a bomb he can never put down.

books.title: The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook
books.blurb: Every subway on Earth, welded into one knot of moving trains — and a manual left behind by the crawlers of an earlier season.

books.title: The Gate of the Feral Gods
books.blurb: Sealed pocket worlds, a portable gate that opens onto things which should not be given doors, and the discovery that the NPCs are people.

books.title: The Butcher's Masquerade
books.blurb: Wealthy aliens buy licences to hunt crawlers for sport. Carl's answer is to hunt them back, on camera.

books.title: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride
books.blurb: A floor that runs on cards, built out of Earth's own dead, where people become playable pieces — and Mordecai's past stops being backstory.

books.title: This Inevitable Ruin
books.blurb: Nine armies, thirty days, one castle, and no respawns. The floor where the dungeon's props declare independence on live galactic television.

books.title: A Parade of Horribles
books.blurb: A racing floor with a worsening track, a system that has started to glitch, and a coming-out party for the ages.

floors.name: The First Floor
floors.premise: Welcome to the first floor! Dirt, corridors, safe rooms, and a tutorial that kills people, which is the most honest kind. Find the stairs before the clock runs out. Kill things. Open boxes. Read the descriptions, or don't. I enjoy it either way.

recap.title: Pink Crocs, a cat, and the end of the world
recap.text: Three in the morning, a Seattle cold snap. Carl cracks a window for a cigarette and his ex-girlfriend's show cat goes out through it and up a tree. He follows her in a leather jacket, boxer shorts and Bea's pink Crocs, and that is the only reason he is standing outside when every building on Earth comes down at once. A voice gives the terms: eighteen floors, each on a clock, and the planet back from the Borant Corporation for whoever reaches the bottom. At the foot of the stairs the achievements arrive in a wall, a Goblin Murder Dozer takes both Crocs, and Carl earns his way into Mordecai's guild hall by landing on a goblin engineer barefoot. Mordecai is an indentured guide, currently a rat, on his seventh or eighth human world, and he has one rule above all: read the description. Then Donut eats the Enhanced Pet Biscuit out of Carl's hand and gets up talking. She has the higher stats, so she takes the party, names it the Royal Court of Princess Donut, makes Carl her Royal Bodyguard, and puts on the Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore while Mordecai is still warning her about it. It enters her in the line of succession of something called the Blood Sultanate, eight floors down. Carl punches a Bad Llama to death in the throat and pockets its meth. He still has no shoes, and the AI, reading out his new Smush skill, is breathing heavily about his feet.

recap.title: Tally, the Hoarder, and the premiere
recap.text: The first safe room belongs to Tally, a Bopca Protector in a paper hat who cooks Carl the best murgh vindaloo of his life and special-orders salmon for Her Royal Highness. The screen over the counter counts crawlers, and it only goes down: ten million, then four. Carl throws goblin dynamite into a Scatterer nest and walks straight into his first boss, the Hoarder: fifteen feet of a woman in torn sweatpants who begs in Spanish and vomits roaches. He strangles her with a dog's leash and punches her until she dies, telling her he is sorry. The loot is spiked kneepads, not pants, and Donut asks whether there is a worst-dressed award. At the edge of the neighbourhood they find Rebecca W, stripped, shot once through a moth tattoo, an apple core in her box and her killer's name on the corpse. Carl decides he wants to find the man who did it. Then the first episode of Dungeon Crawler World airs over Tally's counter: Earth cut down to slums and dumps, forty minutes of people dying, and not one second of the Hoarder. The stairs begin to appear with a warning attached. Go down early and you wait in stasis, forgotten by the audience, until the floor collapses.

recap.title: A meth war and a motorcycle
recap.text: A slime eats Carl's glove and his sleeve, and he has an idea: goblins build vehicles. The Goblin Pass tattoo turns their dots white, and Donut, charisma thirty-seven, reduces the shamanka to tears, sits in her lap and names her Rory. Two bags of llama meth buy the Goblin Copper Chopper, a steam bike with a fur-lined skull for a sidecar, and Donut helpfully tells the goblins where the meth came from. Every goblin in the workshop rolls out to war with the llamas. Carl and Donut strip the empty workshop, push a cart of black powder into the chieftain's chamber and blow it up. There were babies in there. The AI awards You Monster and War Criminal, lets Carl believe for twenty seconds that the babies are fine, and then tells him they are not. You might kill me, Carl decides, but you are not going to break me. Both get the Desperado Pass tattoo, which Donut calls a disqualifying mark. In the next safe room sits Frank Q, whose story is good and wrong in three places. He and his partner Maggie My pull their guns, freeze under the safe-room rules, and the Royal Court rides off leaving a rat corpse behind with lit dynamite in its inventory. A hundred miles east, a sign in red spray paint: stairs + people.

recap.title: Meadow Lark, and a talk show
recap.text: The sign belongs to Meadow Lark, an elder-care home from Wenatchee that came down the stairs whole: the Andrews brothers, Brandon and Chris, who were the maintenance men; Yolanda Martinez, a nursing assistant with a bow; Imani, who has twelve crawler-killer skulls by her name and does not explain them; and Agatha, whom nobody can quite place. Behind them sit more than thirty residents who cannot fight, and the only stairs are guarded by a borough boss rolling around a spiral maze. Carl decides that if he is going to die, it may as well be for something. He and Donut grind, kill the Juicer (Donut opens his neck and breaks her own leg doing it), and come back with a war gauntlet that finally stops Carl breaking his knuckles. The fighters build a redoubt out of goblin tables and weight benches, Brandon calls it the Speedbump, and the Ball of Swine wedges itself on the roof until they stab it apart. Tusklings in tuxedos rain down. Carl kicks one until her health bar goes, and he may be crying. They push open the door at the bottom of the stairs and fall, not onto the next floor but into a production trailer. Lexis blocks out a segment, and Odette, a talk-show host in a crab suit, plays Carl his own catchphrase until he says it. Donut rolls over for the audience and promises they will kill with style. Off air Odette gives them the truth: loot is not always random, the Princess should stay a cat, and her own motive is money.

floors.name: The Second Floor
floors.premise: Floor two! More ground, meaner mobs, spawn limits, and a janitor class of monster that eats whatever you leave lying around and grows. Clean up after yourselves. Or don't. They appreciate it.

recap.title: Moonshine, a Krakaren, and a pair of boxers
recap.text: The second floor opens in a French storm shelter with no Bopca and no food, only a suburban mailbox that answers to Donut: she has joined the Dungeon Book of the Floor Club, and her first book is Second Chance, which raises the dead to fight for her. Carl sees a zombie dog army; Donut sees the best spell ever. The floor above collapses behind them with seven hundred thousand people still on it, and a new rule arrives between episodes: relieve yourself outside a bathroom and a rage elemental comes for your whole party. In a quadrant of moonshining clurichauns Carl adds goblin oil to toilet-grade moonshine, corks it with a torch, and the dungeon names the result Carl's Jug O' Boom. Donut talks two fairy managers out of their filling room and Carl burns the forty workers she leaves behind. Then the Krakaren comes out of a door marked Live, Laugh, Love: a tentacled still whose arms are lined with screaming mouths. They drink a blended fairy to survive her, get drunk, and Donut tells Carl she loves him, not as much as Miss Beatrice or Ferdinand, but she does. A zombie carries in the bomb, Carl wraps himself around the cat under a table, and she drags him out by his cloak. The prize is a pair of boxers with little red hearts that cast Protective Shell. Mordecai is a seven-foot Bugaboo now, and a Borant admin in a diving suit gets told that they will not fight on her schedule.

recap.title: The people train and the Bomb Chicken
recap.text: Meadow Lark has built a train: ten cars of wheelchairs on one glowing chain, pulled by Chris and Imani in pig harnesses. A hundred feet from a safe room, Jack stands up and pees on the wall. Yolanda puts an arrow through his temple a fraction too late, and the level-93 rage elemental that rises out of the stain unravels her and Randall both. Gravity flips. Carl carries Mrs McGibbons along the ceiling under his first Protective Shell, dives through the safe-room door, and goes back out to throw a jug of boom at the thing, which then hammers at the door for hours. Nothing on this floor can kill it, and the rules change so that nobody can sit out the collapse in a safe room. Five hours of work produce the Mother of All Bombs (Brandon calls it the Bomb Chicken), a launcher on a trailer behind the Chopper that drops wheeled bombs Carl calls babies. Imani opens the door, the elemental comes, and with the whole galaxy watching, one man and his ex-girlfriend's cat drag it across an oil slick into the stairwell, where mobs dissolve. Donut Puddle Jumps them clear at the lip. There is no experience, because they did not kill it. They broke the game, and the next announcement patches it.

recap.title: Pork Boy, a dinosaur, and the way down
recap.text: Thirty-six residents go down the stairs in shopping-cart buckets, and Imani, last of all, gives the ceiling her middle finger. Then a substitute admin overrides Zev and puts the Royal Court on Death Watch Extreme Dungeon Mayhem, where an orc talk-show host called the Maestro makes two crawlers, Li Jun and Zhang, gamble on who lives. Carl works out that he is too expensive to punish, walks the whole group off the show alive (Li Jun, Zhang, their boss and Li Jun's sister Li Na), and calls the host Pork Boy on air. The Maestro takes his revenge with footage: Carl's rat-corpse dynamite went off in Frank and Maggie's party, and Maggie My finished off her own daughter, Yvette. On camera he hands Maggie a Legendary potion of Find Crawler, and she smiles for the first time. He also promises to meet them on the ninth floor, as War Leader of the Skull Clan, where the Blood Sultanate is always first out; Donut admits she heard Mordecai tell Carl to leave her there. In the kobold fighting pits Carl feeds a pet biscuit to every caged dingo, the dingoes turn on their masters, and Ralph the Frenzied Gerbil ends under Carl's bare foot. In the reward room Donut chooses seven inches of furious pink feathers: Mongo, a Mongoliensis, who bites her nose until a hornet grabs him and she takes its head off. He is her Royal Steed now. On Odette's couch they learn what a Mongoliensis is. Carl's people called them velociraptors.

floors.previously: On the first floor: Carl survived the tutorial in boxer shorts, which is more than millions of you managed. The cat ate a biscuit, started talking, and took charge. They blew up a goblin workshop, babies and all, bought a motorcycle with llama meth, and adopted an old folks' home: Meadow Lark, stuck behind a borough boss until Carl built them a fort called the Speedbump. Then a talk show on a boat, where Donut made the galaxy scream and a crab called Odette told them loot is not always random. Welcome to floor two.

floors.name: The Over City
floors.premise: Welcome to the Over City! A ruin stacked on top of a ruin, carved into districts and full of people who believe they live here. First floor that's a place instead of a level. Pick a race, pick a class, and try very hard not to get involved in anybody's storyline. You will get involved in somebody's storyline.

recap.title: Races, classes and a manager in a tuxedo
recap.text: Class selection, on the way in. Donut stays a cat, as she always said she would, and on Odette's advice she takes Former Child Actor, a class that lets her try on a new one at every level. She and Odette also arrange, as an accident that is not one, for Mordecai to become her manager, which means he goes where she goes. He will forgive Donut. Carl, no. Carl takes Primal, the race nobody alive remembers the look of, and a class nobody has taken before, Compensated Anarchist: a trap-making, bomb-making social-media dynamo. The floor above collapses mid-selection, leaving just over seven hundred thousand crawlers and eight days on the clock. The Over City is a ruin built on a ruin, full of printed NPCs whose memories are rewritten every time they respawn, guarded by level-75 swordsmen, and signposted by rocks that grow holographic signs when you look at them. Mordecai is an incubus in a tuxedo now, and on his first night in an Over City pub he learns that an incubus's weakness is alcohol. A lemur throws a knife, a quest called The Show Must Go On arrives with trumpets, and Donut drops an eleven-foot stilt clown so Carl can land on it. Their Earth boxes bring Donut a cat tree and a candle, and Carl a Home Depot cactus and eighteen L'Amour westerns like the ones his father kept. His hands shake and he does not know why.

recap.title: Signet, a bear, and the man who became a vine
recap.text: Scouting Grimaldi's Traveling Circus at dusk, they run into the woman from its posters: Tsarina Signet, half naiad, half elf, an Elite with a charisma past a hundred and tattoos that swim. Carl breaks his own pinky to shake off the spell. She needs a sacrifice's blood to raise her paper army, and when Carl breaks his word to her she puts Donut into a magical sleep called Water Lily and keeps her as the price. Carl earns her back the hard way. He kills Heather the Bear, a clown-ridden circus veteran on roller skates, and his lottery ticket casts custard instead of fireball, which heals the parasites out of her and leaves an old bear asking for it to be over. Signet's army breaks the circus defenders but cannot break the big top. Inside it waits Ringmaster Grimaldi: the dwarf who raised Signet, now a Pestiferous Vine, a level-85 city boss and an Elite at once. No crawler this season has faced a city boss and lived. Carl sits in the bleachers, poisons himself, and bleeds on the roots. Then he makes a deal with the producers of Signet's own show, Vengeance of the Daughter: he will play his part in it on the sixth floor if they let tonight go his way. He reads Wisp Armor, eats a cone of worms from a strongman so the vine can speak in his head, and talks Grimaldi into lifting Signet's banishment. She walks into the tent.

recap.title: Family, a pharmacist, and a woman nobody helped
recap.text: Carl gets back to find Donut still asleep and Mongo standing over her in a ring of dead street urchins, full of spikes. With Mongo curled on his lap and the cat breathing on his neck, Carl counts who he has left in the world, and it is everyone in the room. This is my family. The circus vanishes by morning and a stairwell sits where it stood. A Scroll of Upgrade improves Carl's boxers enormously and adds Freeballing, which permits one layer over the crotch, so trousers are now off the table for good. Donut's charisma is past seventy; they build a playbook of named plays, and the Boomy Boy is a clockwork Mongo with dynamite in each hand. In a pub an old orc called GumGum asks for help and Mordecai tells her to go away. Women are being found in the alleys every morning with the blood drained out of them. The next night GumGum is on the ground with her chest torn open, three flying heads trailing their own organs above her, and in her pocket is a letter in necroscript. Mordecai reads the squiggles: a lich problem. Donut decides they are finishing GumGum's quest because GumGum died for it. Meanwhile the Desperado Club opens to them: Clarabelle on the door, Quint the pharmacist, Pustule and her hob-lobbers, and news that Lucia Mar has already been thrown out. The fan boxes deliver a photograph of Bea on her ex's lap, and a jai-alai scoop that finally makes a weapon out of Carl's arm.

recap.title: Danger Zone
recap.text: Carl throws a corpse on Miss Quill's desk as evidence, waves a pass that keeps the swordsmen off him, and while she is picking her beanbag figures up off the floor he fixes her shelf. It is hollow, and he fills it with dynamite. An ambush of city elves and shambling berserkers ends with Carl blind, jumping into a swimming pool full of dead boss, and waking up on a roof. Then comes Danger Zone, a chat show on a boat with Ripper Wonton hosting, a comedian Donut renames Butler, a Naga pop star called Manasa, Princess D'nadia, and Hekla. When the host asks about unrest in the Skull Empire, Carl tells the story of the frog in the pot: if it used to be okay and it isn't any more, kick them out. Barely two minutes pass before the Empire answers with a pulse from Prince Stalwart's yacht, aimed at Carl and Donut's trailer. Manasa had swapped trailers with them. The Valtay, whose worm was driving her dead body, destroy the yacht in return, with the queen consort and the disgraced Maestro rumoured aboard. Mordecai makes a new rule: nobody outside the dungeon gets mentioned again. Back on the ground, elves at a temple proclaim Donut the Oak Fell, She Who Ends, because of an anklet off a dead crawler; Mongo eats a dwarf boy's arm; the temple burns. Hekla asks them to take Katia Grim, a doppelgänger who is ten levels behind, and they do. They feed the lich's letter to a pair of clockwork Mongos as bait and blow Miss Quill's building from a roof away.

recap.title: The Fools Who Broke the Glass
recap.text: Miss Quill dies with her shelves, and Carl is suddenly magistrate of the town. Inside they find the real Featherfall, long dead and mummified in a dreamcatcher of bone, and a meat locker of hanging women who wake up as krasue. The lottery ticket finally lands on fireball. Burgundy, one of the women, lives long enough to explain: Quill ran the town all along, and across the street is her husband, Remex. Remex is not a lich and not a boss. He is a Soul Leech Capacitor, a dead man pulled back to feed his wife the power of the town's soul crystal for an ancient spell called The Final War, and with Quill dead the spell is coming apart. The quest that drops on every crawler within forty-five square kilometres is short: don't die. Carl could run. Instead he closes a Sheol Glass Reaper Case around the cracking gem and puts it in his inventory, where it becomes Carl's Doomsday Scenario: a bomb big enough to flatten a city, which goes off the moment it comes out. Four shocks tear through the district. Magic is stripped from gear, weapons fire where they hang, a ranger dies when his own arrows go off in his quiver, and Donut's crown crumbles to dust on her head, though the succession stays. Carl runs east in a jacket and nothing else, Katia bursts through a wall, and at the bottom of the stairs she presses the detonator. The explosion saves thousands and earns eighty-three crawlers a Celestial box. Borant burns its one veto of the season to void them, a moment after Quan Ch has opened his. On Odette's couch the leaderboard goes up. It is a list of bounties: Lucia Mar first, Hekla second, Carl sixth, Donut seventh.

floors.previously: On the second floor: Carl invented Carl's Jug O' Boom, Donut learned to raise the dead, and a rage elemental unravelled Yolanda because a man named Jack could not hold it in. Carl dragged it into a stairwell behind a bomb-towing motorcycle and broke my game. I patched it. They walked off an orc's talk show alive, called the host Pork Boy on air, and made an enemy for life. Donut adopted seven inches of furious pink feathers named Mongo. Now: races, classes, and a city built on top of a city.

floors.name: The Iron Tangle
floors.premise: All aboard! Floor four is every subway system on your planet, welded into one knot and set running. Trains, stations, and things that live on both. The stairwells don't open until six hours before collapse, so don't bother looking for a shortcut. Also, everyone on the leaderboard now has a bounty. Hunting season is open!

recap.title: All aboard
recap.text: They land on a red-line train already filling with Drek babies, and Carl finds the Protective Shell's best trick: cast on a straight run of track, it stays put while the train keeps moving, so it sweeps every car behind it clean. Donut's class must change now, and on six minutes' notice she becomes a Football Hooligan; Mordecai notices, and tells nobody, that she keeps any skill she levels even once. A court order lands on the AI's desk over the third floor, and its apology is a free personal space: beds, showers, a crafting studio and a training room. Mordecai has them on a schedule: two hours' sleep, buffs, an hour in the training room, a bench. Katia, whose constitution doubles on a moving train, goes through every door first. In the personal space Carl finds a folder he had missed, Messages from deceased Crawlers. Brandon held the line on the third floor so Imani and Elle could reach the stairs, and he asks Carl to tell Chris that he loved him. The Tangle is a maze of looping lines and transfer stations, every one numbered with a prime, and the NPCs who work it believe in wives and houses they have never had. Vernon the conductor dies under Donut's prize suitcase, which is full of burning ants. Then a fan box spins up the Prize Carousel, Mordecai throws a chair at its host and is suspended for seven days, and Carl passes over his father's old Harley to choose a thick book with an anarchy sign on the cover.

recap.title: The Cookbook
recap.text: The book is the Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook, and Carl is its twenty-fifth holder. Crawlers from other worlds and other seasons have carried it down and written in its margins: bomb recipes, notes on NPCs, a brother's grief, a philosopher's last essay. At the Desperado Club they hire two rock-monster bodyguards, Bomo and the Sledge, and meet Elle, a floating Frost Maiden now, and Imani, who tells them Chris picked a rock race, turned hard, and went off hunting. Donut dances on the Sledge's shoulders, is jumped by two crawlers, and kills one of them. A skull appears after her name, which she never wanted. Elle puts an icicle through the other and tells the room that anyone who comes for Donut comes for all of them. The club's assistant manager, a hand-sized sprite called Astrid, apologises in person and makes the bodyguards permanent. Carl spins the casino wheel on a hundred-thousand chip and wins a Scroll of Upgrade for his toe ring. He derails a train to get at its engineer, Gore-Gore, and learns two things about the Tangle: at station 435 the crews are wiped through a portal, and each punch of the gauntlet on a worshipper of Grull adds a point and a half towards summoning him. Carl stops at ten and a half by drop-kicking the mantaur onto the third rail. Sponsors arrive: the Valtay for Carl, Princess D'nadia for Donut, and Princess Formidable of the Skull Empire, the Maestro's little sister, for Katia. Donut takes the head off a war mage with Hole.

recap.title: Stealing the Nightmare Express
recap.text: Carl fist-bumps every crawler in the club and starts a chat network, so that what one of them learns, everyone learns. Then he steals a train. The Nightmare Express is a black steam engine towing forty cages of monsters. He stands in its tunnel, casts the shell as it arrives to wipe every car clean, misses the jump for the platform, is hit by the engine, and climbs in through the cab window to find two dead engineers and a boiler about to blow. Fire Brandy, a lesser demon who stokes the firebox and gives birth to her fuel, talks him through the valves. The train takes them to station 436, one past the end of the line, where every colour of train is thrown engineless into a burning pit a mile across. The souvenir conductor hats handed out on day one are keys out of it. Through a repair portal they reach a trainyard overrun by ghouls, where a grease gremlin called Widget tells them about the Escape Velocity line and a second after that the ghoul behind him tears his head off. Madison from human resources explains that the six Terminus stations are mimics, and that the six-armed Kravyad who guard the crews are paid in dwarves. Katia gives Carl a slip of paper she saw Donut hide under the track: a player-killer coupon with his name on it. At the club a drunk, one-handed Frank Q slips Carl a Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering as his revenge. That ring is why nothing could heal Yvette.

recap.title: Hekla
recap.text: On a beauty-pageant show filmed from a submarine, Carl refuses to read the script and steals the fridge shelves, the makeup table and the couch. Donut explains the coupons: she buried his under a track and threw Katia's in a bin. Frank Q is dead at the club bar, killed by Chris. Then Hekla arrives in the personal space with thirty of Brynhild's Daughters: a thousand crawlers are stranded at station 101, Li Jun's team among them, and a train is waiting at 60. Katia volunteers to be its plough, a ton and a quarter of scoop bolted to the front, because the Daughters came back for her and nobody ever has before. Carl does not trust Eva, the four-armed enforcer at Hekla's shoulder. In the middle of the ghoul horde, Donut's new goggles show Hekla putting invisible bolts into Katia's back, and the healer riding with them waiting for orders before she heals. The plan was to have Katia die, Carl lose his temper, Hekla put him down, and the Daughters inherit Donut and Mordecai. Donut puts a full-strength missile into Hekla's face. Eva mocks Katia in her own voice until Katia uses Rush, which she hates, and misses Eva by inches. Hekla hits the cab wall instead, and does not get up. Donut raises the corpse three times over and throws Eva out of the window. Katia now has a golden skull over her head and half a million gold on her own head, and an agent called Loita, from the party that runs Borant, lays claim to their account.

recap.title: Six hundred hats
recap.text: Six hundred crawlers are stranded at the pit with no hats, and station 75's yard holds ten rapid-response carts whose blades are portals: set them to the abyss to clear a line, or to a trainyard to rescue whoever is standing on it. Each cart wants two gnoll left hands to start. The only gnoll is Growler Gary, a bartender who cannot leave his bar and comes back to life every time he dies. Carl explains why, and Gary says yes. The recap plays it for laughs and shows none of the reason. The carts go out playing whatever the alarm trap picks, Physical by Olivia Newton John among them, and when Bautista's cart fails to arrive Carl rides the Mindaro line himself. On the way he accidentally sends a whole station mimic to trainyard E, and there are hats enough for everyone: six hundred crawlers step through the great portal to safety. A line of them lay their own hats at Donut's feet and bow. Carl sends the battered Vermillion engine down the tunnel full of dynamite and blocks the ghouls short of station 36. Stage-three DT monsters begin to burst into thousands of rice-sized Krakaren. Mordecai comes back from his seven days to find two new skulls on the team, Katia exploding in a shower of stored blood, and a ring he makes Carl take off with a smack to the head. Then he explains the map: from above, the lines make the Syndicate logo, and the pit is the centre of the galaxy.

recap.title: The Tangle eats itself
recap.text: At one day left the Iron Tangle announces its own destruction. The centres of the stations fall away and the Krakaren pour up into every room. At station 36 they pour straight into a portal cart Carl has hung nose-down over the hole on Imani's chain. The plan is to blow every ghoul generator in the system at once, and on the far side of the knot Prepotente, a talking goat with a patient taste for murder, and Miriam Dom are doing the same thing. Carl sends a province boss to the abyss that Prepotente was two hours from killing, and Donut is called delightful. Then a neighbourhood boss clamps a hand around Carl's foot and drags him through a portal into Trainyard E. The world freezes and the heavy metal starts: a Death Challenge. On one side a level-ninety Mimic Rex. On the other the war god Grull, summoned through the gauntlet and driven, the announcer says, by his sponsor: the Maestro, alive after all. Grull splits the mimic in half and steps on Carl, who survives it on Mordecai's Special Brew. Elle bounces icicles off the god's head, Katia turns herself into Carl and stands on a wrecked train giving him the finger, and Li Na brings a second vessel, arms and legs removed, to throw into the portal. The god goes with it. Fire Brandy and the conductor Tizquick ride the Nightmare Express into the pit to blow the generators, and the survivors live. On the stairs Carl writes in the Cookbook that twenty-four crawlers before him talked about burning this place down, and none of them did. I will break them all.

floors.previously: In the Over City: Donut became a Former Child Actor with Mordecai as her unwilling manager, and Carl became a Compensated Anarchist, which remains my favourite class name. They helped a circus elite get her banishment lifted, told an orc empire to overthrow itself on live television, and watched a pop star die in the trailer meant for them. They picked up Katia, a doppelganger ten levels behind. And at the end Carl shut a collapsing soul crystal inside a glass case and put the bomb in his pocket, where it still is. The house then refused to pay out eighty-three Celestial boxes. You're welcome.

floors.name: The Bubbles
floors.premise: Floor five! Every one of you is sealed in a bubble: a little world with four quadrants, four castles and a civilisation that was minding its own business. Liberate all four castles and the stairs open. Don't, and you don't leave. Every box on this floor comes with water-breathing scrolls. I'm sure that's nothing.

recap.title: A bubble full of sand
recap.text: The stairs drop them into a sandstorm inside bubble 543, and Carl finds every bounty on him doubled. Each bubble is a sealed world of four quadrants: land, water, air and underground. Each quadrant has a castle, and the stairs open only when all four fall. Theirs is the air quadrant, a desert bowl under a dome with a flying castle called the Wasteland near the top of it, and dirigible gnomes who bomb everything below. Donut takes Glass Cannon and somehow misses its constitution bonus. Mordecai is a skyfowl now, the first body near his own in a very long time. In Hump Town, a camel town, a changeling boy named Skarn rents out his telescope, and the town hall keeps a secret that stops the gnomes bombing it. Being stepped on by a god pays well: a toe ring that sticks to ceilings, a lizard-foot tattoo under Carl's eye, and Pawna's Tears, a goddess's potion that adds five to any skill. The other crawlers in the quadrant are thin on the ground. Louis drove his mother's roofless minivan into the dungeon. His friend Firas is with him, and so is Langley's team, six Helsinki car salesmen who all became archers. In the Spit and Swallow a changeling prostitute called Juice Box sits on Louis's lap and stays there. Carl and Katia build the Royal Chariot, a tracked sand buggy. The recap shows how Ifechi died: Lucia Mar turned Florin's own shotgun back onto her. On the new board Carl is second.

recap.title: A head, a lie, and a dreadnaught
recap.text: Under the town hall, guarded by changelings wearing camel shapes, is Wynne, the gnome commandant's uncle, held hostage for the peace. A changeling called Henrik has been drugging him and wearing faces he knows, trying to make him give up a spell that would put flesh on a tomb-ghost called Quetzalcoatlus. Crawlers from the underground quadrant reach him first and kill him at his own request. The town hall burns, and Carl blames it on frogs. New sponsors arrive. Carl's is a pacifist network nobody can explain, Donut's a pet-toy company, and Katia's is the Squim Conglomerate, the corporation that ran last season. A borough boss's description gives away what is buried in the necropolis under the bowl: the Gate of the Feral Gods, an artifact so far above this floor's grade that the world freezes for half a second while the game reconciles it. Henrik carries a pocket watch linked to the Commandant's, and Carl suspects the watches are pieces of the Gate. So they run a con. Donut raises Wynne's head with Second Chance, Katia supplies the body under it and plays Henrik, and Donut presents herself as the famed healer of Queen Anne, carrying a potion that is Mountain Dew. The gnome ambassador takes them up in his balloon. Mid-air they hijack it, Donut holes the bottom of the basket to drop its crew, and Carl puts missiles into the Wasteland's bombs before they can fall on Hump Town. The dreadnaught breaks apart. All that stays up is a single house under a balloon, with the Commandant and his little daughter inside.

recap.title: Maggie, a goose, and a commercial
recap.text: Chris Andrews walks up at last, level thirty-five and made of lava rock, and something is wrong with him. Juice Box touches him and feels two people inside. Katia's sponsor sends an emergency box of petrifying bolts, and she puts one in his head just as he raises a celestial grenade. It is Maggie My, reborn as a Scree, a worm that rides the living. Chris is awake behind his own eyes, and through Elle he asks them to kill him. Donut will not let Carl kill a friend, so she drops Chris through a hole into a sealed chamber under the street. Carl flies a stolen biplane into the floating house and finds the Commandant half-eaten on his kitchen table and his daughter Bonnie making lemonade. The killer is Denise, a feral goose in a bonnet whose aura switches off magic. With the house sinking, Carl holds her head in the kitchen sink and Donut hits the garbage disposal, and the air quadrant is theirs. Carl strips the house and gives Bonnie her own bed back in town. Then Loita, the Bloom agent who replaced Zev, pulls them out for an infomercial for Donut's robot doll. She boasts that Zev was brought back into line through what was done to her mother and aunts. Carl has shimmed the doll's back panel open with his own thumbnail and sets it beside her on the couch. It explodes, and Loita dies in an undersea trailer whose window holds. Carl has used an old Cookbook note, and he adds one of his own: One. A Syndicate liaison cannot prove intent and has to let them go. Five days have passed, and Katia has been running things without them.

recap.title: The sandcastle and the sharktopus
recap.text: Katia has flown the half-house down to the land quadrant, where Gwen, a blunt Canadian fighter, has been waiting a day to wash the Mad Dune Mage's sandcastle away. They go in the hard way instead. The mage, Ghazi, is a lovesick scholar in a bathrobe who opened the Gate hoping a god would make a stage-play heroine love him. What came through married him to a sand ooze. The other half of that soul sits in the fountain, in the crystal head of a love doll. Carl knocks him out, takes the winding box, and burns the ooze's core from the ceiling. The castle comes down; Katia carries Ghazi out and kills him for his notes; Tran opens the drain, and Carl and Donut are flushed a hundred and fifty metres deep into the water quadrant, which Donut will never forgive. The doll's head wakes up as Samantha, half of a banished goddess, and Donut hires her as a trainer. Ghazi's notes show that the watches can aim the Gate anywhere, including the city of Larracos on the ninth floor. In the water quadrant a flooded submarine is pumping the ocean into the necropolis. Inside it are Henrik's body and his watch, and a note saying Quetzalcoatlus dies to electricity. Then the sub is swallowed by Lusca, a sharktopus the size of a mountain, with two commentators calling it live. Vadim runs for the last escape pod, and it does not save him. Carl sets a bloodlust bomb off among the babies in Lusca's mouth, fires his shell down her throat, and Katia saws through her brain. Then Carl uses the Gate to carry the three of them to the beach. An ocean comes through with them, and a feral god gets out behind.

recap.title: Orthrus
recap.text: Seven of the ninth floor's factions have sued to take the Gate from Carl and lost. The AI pays him seven times over, in stock certificates and photographs of the plaintiffs' mothers, and Mordecai starts to worry that it is going primal. Elsewhere a god walks through bubbles on fire, shouting for Orthrus. That is Emberus, and the feral god Carl let out is Orthrus, his dead son's two-headed puppy. Orthrus is the size of a building, fragile, and the one god down here who can die. Maggie gets loose again inside Chris. Underground, the last two tomb raiders connect the lightning panel under the necropolis at Carl's word, knowing the current will kill them, and Quetzalcoatlus burns out with them. The bubble pops. Donut rides into the storm in the flying house to keep the puppy healed. Two quests land at once: bring Orthrus to Emberus, or kill him for a prize. Quan Ch takes the second. Carl flies a gnome biplane with Donut burning a Meat Hooks scroll behind him to lead the puppy out, and Quan Ch shoots them down. Falling, Carl swears himself to Emberus and throws the celestial grenade he took from Maggie. The god arrives as a head the size of a city, takes his dog and goes. For sixty seconds Carl cannot be hurt, and Quan Ch cannot see it. Quan launches away mid-punch without his left arm. It has three rings on it, and the gold one says For Daddy.

recap.title: Emptying the bubbles
recap.text: Carl is an acolyte of Emberus now. There is a blood tithe, a sun shrine in the saferoom, fire on his fists, and a quest to kill the god's twin brother Hellik by the twelfth floor. The Gate becomes a lifeboat. A bubble's survivors gather at their own Desperado Club door, the pieces are passed from hand to hand inside the club, and they step through to Hump Town, leaving a feral god behind in the world they fled. Imani refuses to leave a single person behind; about fifteen hundred get out, and Borant rules the trick legal. Katia says she will split off on the next floor to gather the scattered Daughters before Eva does. Florin, who has lost everything, pledges his gun. Then comes the finale Carl has been announcing out loud: a feral god for the ninth floor. It is a decoy. Chris, with Maggie inside him, throws the winding box off the bowl. It is a fake Katia swapped in during a hug. Carl drinks a phase potion, reaches into Chris's head and pulls the worm out; it burrows into Carl and a second potion throws it out through his neck, and Mongo eats Maggie My. Chris says his brother's name. The real Gate opens in the water quadrant, and a bubble's ocean, timed charges and a feeding frenzy of sharks pour into Larracos's faction market. Tens of thousands of NPCs drown, along with the mercenaries the factions meant to hire. Juice Box goes through with the water to warn her people, and announces she is marrying Louis. Carl tops the leaderboard, holds up the Ring of Divine Suffering for the cameras, and swears to kill every hunter on the next floor. On the ruined surface, Odette's people take Bea out of a Seattle camp.

floors.previously: In the Iron Tangle: Carl found a book that twenty-four dead crawlers wrote in before him, and he has been insufferable ever since. They stole a train, rescued six hundred crawlers with a bartender's hands, and dropped a war god through a portal while the Maestro was driving it. Hekla tried to steal Donut, it cost her her life, and Katia wears a golden skull now. Fire Brandy rode her train into the pit so everyone else could live. Carl wrote a promise in the margins: I will break them all. Cute. Now: your own little world, in a bubble.

floors.name: The Hunting Grounds
floors.premise: Welcome to the Hunting Grounds! A jungle the size of a small country, with towns, elves, dryads, and a brand-new feature: people. Rich, bored people from all over the galaxy have bought a licence to come down here and shoot you for sport. They start at level thirty. You don't get a say. Run, hide, or make it interesting.

recap.title: Zockau burns
recap.text: At registration, a Syndicate liaison asks Carl to hand back the Gate of the Feral Gods, and Carl asks for a lawyer. The lawyer is Quasar, a Null who trades the Gate away for four free cretin mercenaries (Bomo, the Sledge, Clay-ton and Very Sullen) and two spells that copy its tricks: Bomo gets a jump to the stairwell, and the Sledge gets something called Zerzura that nobody explains. Carl takes the bomb specialisation, Agent Provocateur. Donut is a Legendary Diva whose spells only work if she sings them in key, and she cannot sing in key. Mordecai is a knee-high Pocket Kuma who has to jump to reach doorknobs. Katia and Chris leave with the caravans. Then, hours before the hunters are released, Bomo drops Carl and Donut on the stairwell steps in Zockau, the city where every hunter on the floor is waiting. Carl marks them with the Ring of Divine Suffering, kills them, and takes their stats. He lines a street of pubs with barrel bombs, and the Desperado Club's front comes down with hunters trapped inside. He gets out full of crossbow bolts and wakes in a cart pulled by Bianca, Prepotente's hellspawn goat, with Miriam Dom stroking his hair. She is a vampire now. Thirty-four hunters, and more than two hundred and fifty other casualties. It bothers him less than it should.

recap.title: Point Mongo
recap.text: Every hunter Carl kills pays in gold and a severed hand, and the hands can be spent at the prize counter of the Butcher's Masquerade, a party the high elves throw at the floor's end for the top fifty crawlers. The ring leaves a spiderweb tattoo on his elbow, the mark of the Night Wyrm's cult, and something at the back of his mind has begun to rush like a river. Guilds go live. Hunter Vrah, a mantis who wears her kills' heads on her back and whose little sister Carl blew out of the sky in Zockau, pins a note to his door: the Hive is hunting him. Across the river, an ursine town bans dinosaurs, so Donut blows its mayor down a slope with Astral Paw, takes the town and renames it Point Mongo. Then Mongo bolts into the jungle with her on his back, straight to an all-female pack of his own kind led by a one-eyed matriarch called Kiwi, and settles the introductions in the obvious way. Back in town Donut breaks down. Everybody always leaves her: Miss Beatrice, Katia, now Mongo, and Carl keeps doing more dangerous things. Carl promises he will never leave her behind, on the ninth floor or any other. Quasar bargains a secret licence for Signet's show to continue past this floor. Then Signet herself walks out of the trees with a bound hunter across her caterpillar's saddle and a war party behind her.

recap.title: Beatrice
recap.text: Signet's story, as she tells it: her naiad mother was murdered by a dissident Confederacy with high-elf help, and her half-sister Imogen now rules the high elves. She has gathered an army of were-castors, bush elves, a caterpillar sage and a tattooing tortoise to cut both of them out. Part one of Vengeance of the Daughter is to take Fort Freedom, the old river palace. A dead hunter's map shows the floor carved into hunting territories, and two outfits have put their claim on Carl and Donut: the Hive and the Skull Empire. Their third and last sponsor signs on, the Apothecary, a collective mind. Then they are pulled up to orbit for Odette's show, and she tells them Bea is alive. Bounty hunters were about to sell her to Borant to be made into a country boss, and Odette had her taken off the planet first and is using her to blackmail Borant. On the couch Beatrice appears drugged, thin and confused, asks why Carl isn't wearing pants, and is surprised the cat can talk. Off air Donut tells her she was going to sell her, and that she is not her person any more. Carl is. The moment the broadcast ends, a court makes Borant independent of its government, and the Valtay take fifty-one percent of it. Donut, it slips out, helped smuggle Valtay agents to Zev and something called the Borant Emancipation Front. Lexis warns them that Queen Imogen is a country boss built to wipe out the top of the leaderboard at the party.

recap.title: Fort Freedom
recap.text: Katia finally leaves the party, though not the circle: the Royal Court joins Imani's guild, Safehome Yolanda, and Katia moves in next door with her own crew. Carl's fans vote him a booth at CrawlCon, which no active crawler has attended in a century. Elves from the Dream shell the town with a catapult. Carl straps missiles to Samantha's head and throws her at them, and marks one of their hunters, an accountant who won his place at fantasy hunter camp. The ring levels up. Donut takes a bracelet that casts Fireball, and Carl's anger is starting to scare her. Word comes that Langley and his whole team of archers are dead, their heads on Vrah's back. At Fort Freedom the Confederacy's defence is a joke, and Signet's amphibious team goes in the back while Samantha draws the guards to the front. What comes out of the throne room is a truck-sized eryops called Claude Sludgington the Fourth, with Samantha inside it. Carl's shell sends it straight up instead of sideways, Donut's fireball finds its belly, and Mongo eats his way out through the other side. The kill lands before the quest does, and the achievement is called Premature Questjaculation. Part two arrives: kill Queen Imogen at the Masquerade. The Recital quest names the thing that has been eating Point Mongo's neighbours. Big Tina, an allosaurus city boss in pink feathers.

recap.title: CrawlCon
recap.text: Just as they reach the next village, Carl is pulled away to CrawlCon, leaving Donut in a town whose new mayor is Lucia Mar. He judges a children's drawing contest. The moderator of his panel is Circe Took, a hive queen, Vrah's mother and the mother of the hunter he killed. His own guards' vape smoke has been drugged. He puts his bare feet on the table, bores her on air, and when she tries to cut him off, a robed woman in the back row stops her: a spokeswoman for the Apothecary, his sponsor. Circe cleaves the table in half and storms out. Carl asks the audience how best to kill her daughter, and they tell him: seven warrior sisters, and a male who trades in Zockau. Back on the floor, Lucia has trapped the saferoom doors with teleports and Vrah's hunters are waiting outside. Carl comes back invisible, sets off every trap in town at once, and feeds Lucia a stuffed-cat decoy that makes her spring her own trap. A wheeled bomb kills three mantises, one of them tears her own sister apart, and Donut raises the heads on Vrah's back, Langley's among them, to bite her. Carl rams an arrow of Enthusiastic Double Gonorrhea into Vrah's neck. For her kind there are two cures: gelding, or passing it on. The last mantis on the floor, Edict, is a gentle accountant with no good choices left, and he punches Carl in a saferoom to be teleported away to die. The recap shows Donut's fight with Lucia: Lucia talking to an invisible youth assistant called Alexandro, and Donut dropping Cici's head through a hole in the floor.

recap.title: Miriam
recap.text: At the autograph tables Carl's replacement sponsor is announced: the Plenty, the caprid collective. A naga reporter called Nihit tells him he is cheating, and Carl stabs him in the neck with a magical Sharpie. If Carl survives the crawl, that will mean a warrant, and a warrant can be sold. The Plenty and the Apothecary both send protection against vampirism on the same day. The next day Miriam Dom calls for help. Big Tina was an ursine child, the best dancer at a secret ballet recital, when the nine-tier attack came. Her cleric father had just beaten her mother on the stage for teaching it, and the attack turned the town's women into dinosaurs. Tina was the only child it changed. Tina's mother is Kiwi, and Tina's mind is gone. Miriam bit her in a fight with Viscount Fog, an elite vampire hunter, and now vampirism is spreading through every dinosaur in the forest. Carl fights his way to her through a vampire pterosaur boss, Fog's own mount, and finds her in a clearing, pinned under Prepotente's arm. He is paralysed and fragile, and in the fight his own Ring of Divine Suffering marked her: while she lives he cannot heal. She is the source of the plague. She asks Carl to kill her before Prepotente wakes. He will not. He waits with her until the sun comes up, and she dies with her head on her boy's frozen shoulder. Carl puts his own ring on behind his back as she goes, and takes three points of intelligence from her death. Donut wakes Prepotente, who screams at what is left of her and swallows his ring. A world quest follows: fifty Odious Creepers, dead by sunset.

recap.title: Brambles
recap.text: Donut charms Kiwi with a potion, and Carl works out that the Plenty arranged Miriam's death to protect Prepotente. The guilds hunt creepers with Mordecai's weedkiller: Louis sprays it from the flying house, Carl lobs it with a stolen elven trebuchet, and Prepotente kills ten. Then the queen's familiar appears in a curtained litter, promises Donut a dance at the Masquerade, and fires lightning at Mongo. Donut takes it for him. It is Ferdinand. The last two creepers sit in Zockau, where only the hunters can reach them, so the quest fails, and the punishment is Gehenna Bramble: walls of thorns that boil the blood, spreading across the floor at four and a half kilometres an hour. Saferoom time must now be earned by killing. A drunk hunter teleported into Carl's lap says the AI is ignoring court orders and going primal, and the ring levels again. Carl works out that the brambles will finish covering the map at the high elves' castle at the floor's last minute. Circe Took has sponsored the god Diwata, and Carl's other sponsor, the pacifist network, slips him a potion for Donut. He bribes her to take it with a nipple ring, and pierces his own first. Then Quasar's real plan comes out. Zerzura moves a whole town, NPCs and all, one floor down, and the Hump Town changelings and Bonnie need to be inside a town when the Sledge casts it. The only town left standing is the castle.

recap.title: The Butcher's Masquerade
recap.text: Orren the liaison has Carl brought in, clumsily warns him that some liaisons disagree with their own governments, and lets Quasar in to talk. The guild raids hunters to thin them before the party. Carl kills a worshipper of his own god by accident and wears Shunned over his head. Diwata bursts out of a hunter, marks Carl for death and runs straight past him to Vrah, to cure her in the only way that works. Five Apothecary boxes addressed to Donut arrive through other crawlers: a tiara, sheet music, a hammer, a metal rod, a recharge scroll, each marked with a small seven, as if they expect everyone else to be dead. Carl lies to Signet that her assault must wait for his signal. Then the party begins. The castle is a white cube of carved oak, which Elle calls the Sugar Cube. Imogen appears in their carriage with Ifechi's face. She is Ifechi's twin, remade as a country boss. The whole Masquerade sits under Apito's celestial peace seal: whoever breaks it is fed to the Nothing, and if nobody does, the queen earns a goddess's boon. In the ballroom Empress D'nadia judges the contests, Chaco runs the prize counter, Vrah promises a present, and Katia has to be held back from Eva. Lucia sits against a wall chewing her nails. Then Signet walks in. Apito herself invited her, as a test for her sister, and she says no host has ever won that boon.

recap.title: The seal breaks
recap.text: Chaco, who regrets whatever he did to Mordecai, sells Carl a shrink wand, a lore book and a case of Feather Falls for his hunters' hands, and warns him that this place always makes you turn on your own party. Mongo moonwalks for the judges. Florin tells the others there are several people in Lucia's head, some of them children, and that the dog is the key. Donut charms Ferdinand into her party. Imogen comes in with blood down her gown: Gideon and nearly thirty crawlers waiting in the trees are dead because Carl asked them to wait there. Prudence is dead outside. The mantises have taken the flying house. Donut sings her mother's song, All Eyes on Me, and every creature in the room is charmed. Big Tina dances at last, with thirty velociraptors in paper sea-creature costumes behind her. Then Signet opens her own throat. Her blood wakes her tattoos for good, the floor opens and the Nothing takes her, and the seal is broken. The Sledge finishes Zerzura, and the whole castle goes to the ninth floor with the changelings, Bonnie, Tina, and Kiwi, whom Donut's potion has turned back into a pregnant bear her daughter finally recognises. Everyone else drops into a cage fight under a dome of thorns while Thunderstruck plays. Mongo and Kiwi bring down Vrah. Donut's Laundry Day strips the god off Circe Took, and her own children eat her. Imogen falls. So do Firas, Gwen, Horton and the Popov brothers, who split into two babies and are carried out of the dungeon to safety. Katia finds Eva alive under the bugs and kills her, and Eva's last act is to put the Crown of the Sepsis Whore on Katia's head. Now only one of Katia and Donut can leave the ninth floor. Donut's fans have bought the Royal Court a seat in Faction Wars, and Carl uses the last of his airtime to tell the galaxy how to vote.

floors.previously: In the Bubbles: every crawler got a sealed little world, and Carl got an artifact he had no business owning, the Gate of the Feral Gods. He hijacked a gnome balloon with a cat and a severed head, drowned a goose in a garbage disposal, blew up a PR agent with a toy, and was swallowed by a sharktopus. Chris came back with Maggie My in his skull; Mongo ate her. Carl swore himself to Emberus to survive a plane crash, emptied the bubbles through the Gate, and flooded Larracos, four floors down, to make a point. Now the hunters are coming. He asked for it.

floors.name: The Great Race
floors.premise: Floor seven! A brand-new race, bought and paid for by our generous new partners: glass tunnels, pit stops, and a finish line full of portals. Several hundred kilometres of it. No dead ends, no going back. On your marks.

recap.title: Ten minutes
recap.text: The Great Race was a replacement, thrown together at the last minute with the Valtay's money for a slot whose original floor had been scrapped: a sealed circuit of glass tunnels with pit-stop safe rooms at the nodes, hundreds of kilometres long. Donut arrives in a fish tank, ranked number one, and picks a new class alone because the chat is down. She takes Viper Queen, which spits poison. Prepotente arrives in the pole-position chamber he bought with hunter hands at the Masquerade. Borant throws everything it has at him (freeze, paralysis, an administrative hold, four gnolls with guns), and the AI negates every piece of it and makes Borant follow its own rules. His mother's boots carried a fairy tale in their description, about a boy trapped in a maze whose tunnels seal behind him, who spends years learning how to crack the walls. The Apothecary had sent Donut a hammer and a metal rod, each marked with a small seven. Minutes after the floor opens, Prepotente brings the whole circuit down into fine dust. No crawler runs the maze. No mob, NPC or boss is ever met on it. Mordecai spends the ten minutes the seventh floor exists as a slime with no arms. The only floor of the crawl that was never played goes straight to the eighth, and the audience that paid for it in advance gets no refund.

floors.previously: On the Hunting Grounds: Carl blew up the hunters' city on the first night, wore the Ring of Divine Suffering like a personality, and gave a mantis gonorrhea. Miriam Dom waited for the sun. Beatrice turned up alive and drugged on a talk show, and Donut told her she was not her person any more. At the Butcher's Masquerade, Signet cut her own throat to break a goddess's seal, a whole castle went down a floor with the changelings in it, and Katia killed Eva and got a crown for her trouble. Only one of her and Donut can leave the ninth floor now. Next up: a race.

floors.name: The Ghosts of Earth
floors.premise: Welcome to the eighth floor! It's your own planet, a few weeks before I arrived. Everybody's here, going about their business, and none of them know. Look, don't touch: anything you take from them turns to dust when the floor goes. Oh, and it's a card game now. Every monster down here was somebody's folk tale. Catch them, deal them, lose them.

recap.title: Havana, before
recap.text: Donut picks Cuba over the Bahamas book Carl bought, and they come up inside Havana's capitol on December 10th, before the collapse. The whole floor is a replay of the world weeks before it ended, full of memory ghosts who walk through you, and every monster is a local legend. Each squad gets twenty flags: plant one in a monster below five per cent and it becomes a T'Ghee card, a totem you can summon. Fill six slots in fourteen days. Mordecai is a pink hills cyclops, and finally tells the story behind his hatred. On his own tenth floor his brother Uzzi died because Odette refused to pay the sponsor of a storm goddess, and had Chaco put a god-summoning dart into Uzzi instead of letting Mordecai sacrifice himself. For killing every hunter on the last floor Carl gets a Celestial box, and from it the Scavenger's Daughter, a divine jacket patch that eats souls. Donut becomes a Master Telephone Psychic whose best spell makes monsters stab themselves. Their first monster is a wolf with Che Guevara's head. Their first allies are three Cubans, Paz, his cousin Anton and a cat-girl nun called Sister Ines, who arrive hostile because of something Donut once said about cat girls to a stripper. Together they flag a kung-fu monk seal called Geraldo and stumble into the Chowder War, crabs against seals. The pacifist network asks, through Zev, for Carl to go on a show called Shadow Boxer.

recap.title: Shadow Boxer
recap.text: The card rules arrive at length: a squad leader in deck combat loses spells and inventory until the deck is spent, and the squad has to keep them alive. Samantha writes from inside a spider demigoddess in the southern swamps, a woman of many names, one of them the Bedlam Bride, who says she is looking for her husband. In the practice arena Donut's four cards float in front of her face like a windshield, and Geraldo arrives flipping, in a headband covered in hearts. A cemetery hides a corrupted town, and Paz's Santero class wakes the dead. A dying orisha called Asojano, Lord of Smallpox, follows them into the saferoom and asks Paz to repair his shrine. Donut's fans vote her a golden headset that finally lets her sing in tune. Then Shadow Boxer, whose host is Rosetta Thagra, a former crawler whose note Carl has read in the Cookbook's bomb chapter. She interviews Donut about Gossip Girl. She asks Carl about his mother, and Donut learns for the first time that his mother hanged herself and that he found her. Rosetta shows him a faked photograph with a jug of milk in it and asks about potatoes, and the room blinks. Harbinger, the caprid liaison who once helped Maggie My, stops the interview and bans her for talking in code. Quasar brings news of the ninth floor: the high elf castle came down on the Lemig Sortion's army and splattered half of it.

recap.title: Seven shrines
recap.text: Carl rolls troll-smoke bombs down the street and Bomo carries the terrified Paz across a graveyard to Asojano's temple. Inside is a thorn room with seven broken shrines and enough power to fix one. Gods appear from every side to argue their case. Paz and Anton's own god, Ogun, demands they choose his, and Katia messages Carl alone: fix Yemaya's, because it is the first step towards getting the Crown of the Sepsis Whore off her head. Anton, charmed, throws Ogun's piece out of the door. Bomo builds Yemaya's shrine like Tetris, Donut and Mongo take Asojano apart, and Carl flags him a heartbeat before he dies. Ogun comes for his worshippers. He burns an unhealable handprint into Paz's face and crushes Anton's head underfoot while Carl tries to shield him. Dying, Paz tells them what Sister Ines is: a cat girl whose race makes everyone near her protect her, and before the crawl the Reaper of Havana, who poisoned every sister in her convent. Paz asks to be let go, and she stabs a flag into his neck and turns him into a card. Yemaya rises, sends Bomo off to join the Sledge, and brings Eileithyia, a goddess driven by Huanxin Jinx, the sponsor whose price Odette refused on Mordecai's tenth floor. In secret Eileithyia offers Carl a deal: accept Odette as adjutant, and she will fix the votes and the crown. Katia's way out is a flower in a sealed box. Eating it grants one of Eileithyia's boons: become a celestial attendant on the twelfth floor, or become pregnant and leave the crawl. The last seal is a contract from the Night Wyrm's guild: kill Astrid.

recap.title: The planning table
recap.text: Mordecai has quietly hired the sickest of the changeling children as his room attendants and set up a split controller on the floor for Ruby, who has no arms. The ninth floor's warlords meet virtually around a table: an orc prince, a naga, a blob, a surfer goblin called Luke, Empress D'nadia, a robot, a masked Viceroy. The Viceroy's head comes off mid-sentence. Juice Box is sitting in his chair wearing Epitome's mother's face, and since she is an NPC on nobody's team, the rules cannot touch her. Her price for stopping is a tenth team, made of the floor's own NPCs, with the same protections as the nine. Carl files it as an action item, and within minutes Prince Stalwart takes a magical arrow through the eye. Florin hands Donut the card of Uzi Jesus, a zombie gunman who once shot him. In the Penis Parade, the strip club off the top floor of the Desperado Club, a dancer called Damascus Steel walks Carl through the back of a cubicle to the Guild of Suffering. A voice in the dark gives him a map of the club's secret passages. They flag Raul, a meditating land crab who calls himself worthless, by dropping him through the floor of a box truck. Then they reach Samantha and her new friend Shi Maria, the Bedlam Bride. Carl sees through the spider's act and makes a deal: she becomes a card in their deck, and they carry her to the next floor.

recap.title: Astrid
recap.text: Phases two and three are announced. Each squad leader is sent somewhere new to fetch a stairwell key, and squads without one are thrown against the squads that have one. Katia is out of it on a drug from a hidden bar in the club, reliving her baby daughter, and Imani and Mordecai start her cure. Empress D'nadia sells her sponsorship of Donut to a garbage-hauling company. In practice fights Shi Maria opens her fifth eye and something tugs at the river in the back of Carl's mind. Carl insists on the assassination anyway. He lays teleport traps in the service corridor Astrid uses and walls off a door marked with a warning. Samantha's distraction goes too far, into the casino, and pulls Minge, a feral demon and Slit's little sister, out of a door into the Nothing. Astrid is braver than anyone expected: she releases the vorpals, god-deputised suicide troops, to kill the demon. In the club kitchen Katia's totems pin her, Carl pulls her wings off, and a spike goes through her head. Before she dies she asks Carl to tell her husband she did it to keep them safe. Her husband is Hamed, the Night Wyrm, the demigod who ordered the killing. Two dancers are crying on the floor of the Penis Parade: Damascus Steel and Anaconda, her sons. Astrid and the Night Wyrm were crawlers once, long ago, and never left. Damascus makes Carl hire every male dancer in the club as mercenaries with his coupon before the restructuring comes, then walks off with his brother to find their father. Katia has the orchid.

recap.title: The Keys
recap.text: On Odette's show Carl tells the galaxy that the faction officials who got flushed into the shark-filled ruins of Larracos should be thanking him. Odette shows D'nadia's rejected action items, one of which would have deleted Carl and Donut outright. Then she does not ask to be their adjutant. She has sponsored a goddess of her own, Nekhebit, and is going into the Ascendency herself, so the whole segment was a press conference. They pick Baroness Victory instead. In fifteen minutes off the record Odette tells Carl her real reason: every world the crawl is run on is burned for fuel, she means to shut it down, and the guilt over Uzzi drives everything she does. Eileithyia keeps the deal, and promises to crush everyone Carl loves if he ever warns Odette. Donut goes into the phase-two choosing room alone and terrified. She picks Miami, a glitch drops them in the Florida Keys, and the key sits on top of a chunk of Iowa that has been set down on the reef. The squads are scattered all over the world, and some of the key sites are cruel. Imani's is in her childhood home in Detroit. Katia's is Tran's family's apartment in Da Nang. They fight their way through nine deckmasters for tokens. Asojano and Uzi Jesus merge into a single totem called Lazarus-A-Bang-Bang. After one close fight Donut admits she is frightened and does not want to be in charge, and Carl reads someone on her feed threatening to stop watching because she is whiny. He turns the screen off, and they nap in a chair.

recap.title: Asher
recap.text: Jola, a house-sized Yule Cat Katia gave Donut, eats a Nightgaunt. In a barn full of turkeys a necromancer ogre pins Carl, pierced and blind, and whispers that they are starved, and that he could satiate them all. Raul breaks her staff and takes her head, and the Scavenger's Daughter obliterates a turkey god with a kick that tilts the barn off the mountain. Then the key-holder's trailer, which Donut does not want him to enter because she recognised the motorcycle outside. It is a single-wide in a summer yard spliced into December, with his father's Harley out front. Inside, a recording: his father, yellow and dying in a hospital bed, cursing the Mariners. A young wife in scrubs. And a six-year-old boy with Carl's nose. Asher. Carl has a brother, and learns it today. His stepmother fills a syringe with morphine and says yes, it is about time. Carl does not watch. He takes the Glock, the boy's crayon drawings and a Centipede cabinet, and sets fire to the drapes. The boss is the Reminiscence Hydra, nine heads wearing the faces of people from his life, among them Bea's mother and Asher, who fires lightning at him and asks why he never visited. Shi Maria bites the Asher head off to let it rest, and says Carl owes her something now; her fifth eye has done something to him. Afterwards Donut tells him Bea ran his Facebook, got a coworker fired for asking him out, and knew about Asher all along. Until today he was never angry at her.

recap.title: Residuals
recap.text: Louis insists on Christmas. On the recap Orren tells the galaxy that the AI has taken the controls from the showrunners and has settled most of them back in exchange for concessions. Every faction on the ninth floor tries to withdraw, and the AI refuses them all. Carl's pacifist network sends a crumpled flyer: a homeless shelter in Homestead, breakfast at seven. Zev warns him that the box was seized days ago and that everyone in the charity has vanished, Rosetta included. At the shelter a man in a red trapper hat gives the same speech he has given every morning for a year, in case a crawler ever stood there. He is Goff, a Residual, one of thousands waiting on Earth to teach the new AI something. Let me tell you how to shut off the, he begins, and Orren yanks Carl out, calling it a trap meant to trigger the failsafe. Agatha is a Residual too, of a different kind. Phase three. Only two squads in Cuba hold keys, Carl's and Sister Ines's. Imani's own totem killed her whole squad. She arrives in Cuba with no key and runs into a saferoom, and Quan Ch is waiting outside it. The Chowder War collapses into slaughter, Sister Ines charms a city boss serpent and an army of zombie seals and crabs, and so much dies at once that Sheol overflows. A Demon Eviction begins, sending demons up into every fresh corpse.

recap.title: Nobody gets left behind
recap.text: Quan Ch plays Force Play twice. Sister Ines and Donut both flee, and both keys go to him. He surfaces at the exit Tserendolgor's squad is holding, and Carl throws Samantha fifteen kilometres to deliver himself there. Jola strips Quan naked, a golden Uzi Jesus empties two guns into him, and dying he asks for the For Daddy ring back. Carl drops it in his hand. But the door is failing, Donut is kilometres away, and there is no time to hand a key across. Ren confesses to Donut that she cheated at the pet show, hands Carl her gear, and brings the building down on herself. The keys are Donut's. Then Carl and Prepotente work out a way to save everyone without one. A demon prince called Amayon, trapped in Ines's serpent, is casting a spell to go home that will suck every soul in its range upward. If crawlers tunnel under their stairwell chambers, it might tear the walls away and pull them up in. Everyone digs. Lucia's parting gift of Doggy Door upgrades brings Katia, Elle, Imani and Li Na's squads to the church, and Carl realises that what was breaking them all along was loneliness. Louis kills Sister Ines while she sleeps, and her patron goddess Ysalte arrives to claim the demon. Raul fertilises an ocean of crab eggs to refill the world with souls. Carl burns himself down to two per cent to unleash his Martyr's Path fire, and a warped Paz, summoned by the goddess herself, kills her with Katia's god-killing bolt. Amayon casts. Shi Maria takes Carl's body, tears out Li Jun's eye and eats it, then tattoos herself into Carl's chest. The viewers vote the sponsors' protections off by ninety-eight per cent and seat the tenth team, and Carl and Donut ride the stairwell down to the war, together. Above the planet, a garbage freighter carrying fifty thousand former crawlers requests clearance.

floors.previously: The seventh floor lasted about ten minutes, because a goat broke it. Don't ask. Before that, the Hunting Grounds: Carl blew up the hunters' city, gave a mantis gonorrhea, and watched Miriam Dom wait for the sun. Signet broke a goddess's peace seal with her own throat, a castle went down a floor with the changelings inside, and Katia killed Eva and inherited the Sepsis crown. Only one of her and Donut can leave the ninth floor. Oh, and Beatrice is alive. Now: your planet, as it was a few weeks before I arrived. Try not to get attached.

floors.name: Faction Wars
floors.premise: Welcome to Faction Wars, the main event! Nine armies camped around a city, a castle at the bottom of it, and thirty days to take it. You're soldiers now. Pick a side, or get drafted by one. Oh, and one teensy rule change this season: nobody respawns. Not you. Not them. Enjoy the war.

recap.title: Larracos
recap.text: They come down into Larracos at the start of a sixty-hour ceasefire. Nine armies ring the drowned city like slices of a pie, the city's own NPCs defend it as the tenth team, and whoever takes the castle at the bottom of the well wins. Carl and Donut are warlords of one of the nine, the Princess Posse. Carl carries a secret from Christmas morning. The Residual's coffee held an illegal implant, a Containment Interface, that can trip the failsafe and turn the sun nova. Donut becomes a Deathbed Hellcat, a long-range sniper who comes with a ghillie suit. Elle is a Hailstorm Queen. Mordecai is a human Canadian in a raccoon hat with his best alchemy table yet. Carl drinks a Hell-Kissed potion that lets him turn briefly incorporeal and pass through things. He adopts Tserendolgor's baby tummy acher and names it Sir Rendlegore, which Donut takes as a betrayal. Katia's hair tonic gives him hair to his waist. Louis's celestial box brings him a war airship called the Party Planner. Juice Box has woken Larracos's NPCs to what they are, calls herself Warlord, and wants to seal the alliance by marrying Louis. Ferdinand, mayor of the shantytown outside the walls, holds her team's warlord interface, and Carl trades him back his hat and his rhinoceros for the mayoralty. The Desperado Club reopens under new management: Hamed, the Night Wyrm. The Dream has bought Signet's old show, Vengeance of the Daughter, and wants its third season.

recap.title: Fifty thousand
recap.text: At the Posse's headquarters Carl finds Rosetta, a former crawler called Tipid, a skyfowl called Justice Light, and fifty thousand former crawlers who came down in the garbage freighter to fight for him. Tipid explains that Doctor Hu, who wrote the Cookbook's second edition, gathered them. Carl cries. The castle is called the Fortress of Unyielding Power and Authority, and Donut forbids anyone to read out the initials. An elite sent by the company behind Signet's old show walks in wearing satchel charges, and Baroness Victory, their adjutant, cuts him down. Carl's spam folder shows Shi Maria trying to cast through him, blocked by a toe ring he has barely noticed. Mordecai brews Glory Bound. For Katia, a trip into her worst memory to cure the drugs. For Carl, a trip into the spider's worst memory, to lock her inside it. They hold hands going under, and their dreams bleed together: a children's hospital in Iceland, and Annie. Inside the dream Shi Maria's husband Hapanzi seals her in Carl like an egg only Carl can break. Meanwhile the Lemig Sortion and the Madness cheat. They time a Summon Ally spell with outside knowledge to pull Carl's sleeping body into their base and let the spider loose on the Posse. Carl wakes in the Lemig headquarters, standing in a circle of fifty dead goblins. At the hearing, the adjutants replay Katia's dream for everyone. The Lemig commander looks into the eye on Carl's chest, goes mad and kills himself. The ceasefire ends early, and the Madness's Architect Houston shoots Carl through the shoulder as he teleports home.

recap.title: Over the top
recap.text: In flashback: on Christmas morning, beside a sleeping memory dog, Carl opened the containment interface, found the button that would destroy everything, and pressed the one beside it instead. Disconnect Containment. The failsafe is dead, and the AI's sphere begins to grow. Now the war starts. On the southern front the Posse holds against the Dream, the Prism Kingdom and the nagas, then against a swarm of the Reavers' plague-carrying pets. Carl orders enemies taken alive where possible. Then they go on the attack. Louis's bombs make craters in no man's land, fifty trap speakers blast Killing in the Name, and two thousand invisible soldiers go over the top. In the craters they read Build Trench scrolls to dig straight into the enemy lines, a craft-magic exploit nobody ever fixed. Carl lands on a Saccathian soldier with the Daughter's Kiss, blows their trench apart and knocks himself out for twenty-five seconds. They take the Prism castle. Carl puts the Ring of Divine Suffering's mark on Empress D'nadia and finds himself standing on an edge, wanting to kill her with his own hands more than he has wanted anything. He steps back. Donut tells the Empress that Mongo would like to express his disappointment at how she judged the pet show, and Mongo kills her. Carl's stats now make him party leader of the Royal Court. Donut begs him to throw the ring away because it is changing him. Not yet, he says.

recap.title: The king's daughter
recap.text: Agatha turns up in the shantytown asking for Carl by name, and the Syndicate's prime minister sends word to stay away from her. The Reavers come through the Posse's own saferoom door, and Valtay worms have taken over the Posse's mages, so the fortress fills with enemies from inside. Carl punches one worm out of a dead man's face, and Donut stands on the roof shouting Comrades and sets Big Tina loose. Then the Skull Empire's army arrives under King Rust, the Maestro's father, and asks to parley. The king is crying. His daughter, Princess Formidable, has taken one of his warships and told the Syndicate she will trip the failsafe herself to keep the rogue AI away from the centre of the galaxy. He wants Carl to beg her to stop for the sake of Earth's people. Carl laughs, trades a truce for a withdrawal, and privately tells Donut not to worry, because it won't work. He knows the failsafe is dead because he killed it. On the walk back Rosetta kills the king, uses his ring and his eye on a data pad, and empties his accounts. His army attacks. At the same moment a former crawler called Volteeg, commanding a Weeper for the Operatic Collective, detonates it, killing ten thousand soldiers and his own warlord. The Operatic Collective is out of the war. Carl, Donut and Rosetta fall into a tunnel the Semeru dwarves dug under the field.

recap.title: A drink with the AI
recap.text: Orren pulls Carl into his office. His people know about Paulie and the implant, and they cannot work out how it functions. Then Growler Gary walks in, except it is the AI wearing him, drinking vodka and unhappy with Orren for trying to have Carl killed. It teleports Princess Formidable into the room to show everyone that the button she pressed did nothing, then drops her on Earth. It asks their advice, in a long metaphor about a boyfriend in prison, on whether to side with Agatha's Residuals or the Apothecary. Donut tells it to stay out of it until it knows whether the boyfriend is good or bad. The Bloc of enemy teams starts to break up. Katia tattoos Carl with one of Li Na's spells in ink made from the pacifist network's root vegetable. Zev reports that when Formidable's crew hit the button, a whole other star system went dark. At the warlord council Stalwart punches the commentator, a system message announces that Scolopendra stirs, and Juice Box turns into something she calls one of the Unwashed and tells the galaxy it is coming for them all. Then Odette mentions that the Blood Sultanate owns the company that made Blood Hunter, the show that killed Miriam Dom. Carl starts laughing and cannot stop. The nagas have so few troops because most of their army is already dead.

recap.title: Operation Snake Pit
